reconstructed_theorem_text: For every measurable space W, complete real inner-product normed vector space H, measures mu,nu on W, feature:W->H, and label:H, assume feature is genuinely Bochner integrable under mu and under nu. Set m=integral_W feature dmu, n=integral_W feature dnu, potential(w)=2*inner_product(m-label,feature(w)), and D=integral_W potential dnu-integral_W potential dmu. Then all six claims hold: potential is integrable under mu; potential is integrable under nu; D=2*inner_product(m-label,n-m); norm(n-label)^2-norm(m-label)^2-D=norm(n-m)^2; norm(m-label)^2+D<=norm(n-label)^2; and t->norm(m+t times (n-m)-label)^2 has genuine real derivative D at t=0. The two supplied assumptions are vector integrability; scalar integrability and all pairing and loss identities are derived. No probability, finite-mass, sigma-finiteness, equal-mass, or normalization condition is imposed on the measures. The vectors are literal integrals rather than normalized means. D is a difference of genuine real integrals of the same potential anchored at m, never an integral against positive or truncated subtraction of measures. The unhalved loss gives exact potential factor 2 and remainder coefficient 1. Only the displayed affine vector-space curve is differentiated; no measure-valued curve identification or measure-functional derivative is asserted.
objects: W,H; measures mu,nu; vector-valued feature and fixed label; unnormalized vector integrals m,n; scalar potential anchored at m; scalar difference D; affine H curve.
domains: W is measurable. H is a real inner-product normed space with an explicit CompleteSpace hypothesis. mu,nu:Measure W are arbitrary. feature:W->H; label:H. Vector and scalar Bochner integrals range over all W with their indicated measures; derivative parameter t is real.
quantifiers: Universally quantify W,H,mu,nu,feature,label. Given Integrable(feature,mu) and Integrable(feature,nu), all six conclusions hold for the fixed let-definitions. Only real t varies in the last curve and the derivative is at zero.
assumptions: Supplied: the stated structures including completeness of H, and genuine feature integrability under each measure, including its respective almost-everywhere strong measurability. No scalar potential integrability, feature second moment, label bound, mass restriction, or differentiability premise is assumed.
conclusion: Integrable(potential,mu) and Integrable(potential,nu); D=2*inner_product(m-label,n-m); exact squared remainder norm(n-m)^2; supporting inequality norm(m-label)^2+D<=norm(n-label)^2; and derivative D at zero of the displayed affine-curve squared loss.
scopes: m,n are unnormalized actual feature integrals. Potential pairs m-label with feature(w), not feature(w)-label, and remains the same in both scalar integrals. Subtraction is nu minus mu, matching n-m. The nonnegative squared remainder yields the support inequality; D itself need not be nonnegative. Genuine supplied integrability justifies all integral values. The derivative is only a scalar-parameter derivative along an affine H curve, with no asserted identification with measure interpolation or a first variation on measures.
constant_dependencies: There is exactly coefficient 2 in potential and pairing, and coefficient 1 on unhalved losses and the squared remainder. No averaging denominator, unknown constant, or measure normalization is introduced.
